3 Days First-time visitors April through October

3 Days in Berlin

The classic first-timer plan: Mitte landmarks on day one, Berlin Wall history in Kreuzberg on day two, Charlottenburg and the Tiergarten on day three.

Day 1

Mitte: landmarks back to back

Brandenburg Gate, Reichstag, Museum Island. Berlin's must-sees sit close enough together that the whole day works on foot.

  1. ☀️
    Morning
    9:00am – 10:30am

    Start at Brandenburg Gate

    Pariser Platz, the Hotel Adlon and the Holocaust Memorial are all right here. Give the first half hour to standing around and getting your bearings.

    📍 Brandenburg Gate 🏙️ Mitte
    💡 Tip: Café Einstein Unter den Linden, a Berlin breakfast institution, is a five-minute walk.
  2. ☀️
    Morning
    10:30am – 12:00pm

    Reichstag dome

    Norman Foster's glass dome over the German parliament. Entry is free, but nobody gets up there without registering first.

    📍 Reichstag
    💡 Tip: Register online at bundestag.de at least a week out, and bring the same photo ID you signed up with.
  3. 🍽️
    Lunch
    12:30pm – 2:00pm

    Lunch on Gendarmenmarkt

    Berlin's handsomest square: the Konzerthaus flanked by the German and French domes. Restaurants line the side streets.

    📍 Gendarmenmarkt
  4. 🚶
    Afternoon
    2:00pm – 6:00pm

    Museum Island

    Large parts of the Pergamonmuseum are closed for renovation, so aim for the Neues Museum and the Nefertiti bust instead. One area ticket covers all five houses.

    📍 Museum Island
  5. 🌆
    Evening
    6:00pm – 7:00pm

    TV Tower at sunset

    The deck sits 666 feet (203 m) above the city. Book a timed slot; the sunset ones go first.

    📍 TV Tower Alexanderplatz
  6. 🍷
    Dinner
    8:00pm

    Dinner at Hackescher Markt

    The courtyards around Hackescher Markt hold a dense run of restaurants, most of them modern German rather than traditional.

    🏙️ Mitte
Day 2

Berlin Wall history and Kreuzberg

East Side Gallery, Checkpoint Charlie, Görlitzer Park. A walking day through the years the city was split in two.

  1. ☀️
    Morning
    9:30am – 11:30am

    East Side Gallery

    0.8 miles (1.3 km) of the original Berlin Wall, painted with 105 murals in 1990, running along the Spree river. Go early; the crowds build after lunch.

    📍 East Side Gallery 🏙️ Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg
  2. 🍽️
    Lunch
    12:00pm – 1:00pm

    Markthalle Neun

    A covered market hall from 1891. On Thursday evenings it runs Street Food Thursday, with stalls from a couple of dozen kitchens.

    🏙️ Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg
  3. 🚶
    Afternoon
    2:00pm – 3:30pm

    Checkpoint Charlie + Wall Museum

    The old crossing between the American and Soviet sectors. The guard house is a replica; the escape stories in the Mauermuseum next door are the real substance.

    📍 Checkpoint Charlie
  4. 🚶
    Afternoon
    4:00pm – 6:00pm

    Walk through Kreuzberg 36

    Bergmannstraße, Görlitzer Park, Oranienstraße. Kreuzberg 36 is the old West Berlin postal code, and this Kiez, the local word for a neighborhood you can walk end to end, is Turkish and punk at the same time.

    🏙️ Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg
  5. 🍷
    Dinner
    8:00pm

    Dinner in Kreuzberg

    From currywurst at a sidewalk stand to Michelin stars, Kreuzberg covers every price bracket inside a few blocks.

Day 3

West Berlin and the Tiergarten

Charlottenburg Palace, the Kurfürstendamm and KaDeWe: the half of the city that stayed western, ending with a walk back through the Tiergarten.

  1. ☀️
    Morning
    9:30am – 11:30am

    Charlottenburg Palace

    The largest surviving Prussian palace in Berlin. The baroque garden behind it is free to walk.

    📍 Charlottenburg Palace 🏙️ Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf
  2. 🍽️
    Lunch
    12:30pm – 2:00pm

    KaDeWe gourmet floor

    The sixth floor of KaDeWe is a food hall built around counters: oysters, sushi, pasta, Berliner Buletten (local meatballs). Eat standing up like everyone else.

    📍 KaDeWe
  3. 🚶
    Afternoon
    2:30pm – 4:00pm

    Kurfürstendamm + memorial church

    The city's window-shopping boulevard, 2.2 miles (3.5 km) end to end. The bombed-out Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church, left as a ruin on purpose, anchors the eastern end.

    📍 Kurfürstendamm
  4. 🚶
    Afternoon
    4:30pm – 6:00pm

    Tiergarten walk

    Berlin's green middle, from Zoo station back toward the Brandenburg Gate: about 2.5 miles (4 km), roughly 50 minutes at an easy pace.

    📍 Tiergarten
  5. 🍷
    Dinner
    8:00pm

    Farewell dinner in Mitte or on the Ku'damm

    Pick whichever end is closer to your hotel. Both have plenty of options for a last night.
